lines.text: If the Moon vanished tonight, tides would shrink to about a third.

parts.tts: If the Moon vanished tonight, tides would shrink to about a third.
parts.heard: If the moon vanished tonight, tides would shrink to about a third.

lines.text: Relax, it's only a thought experiment. Here's what scientists say would happen.

parts.tts: Relax, it's only a thought experiment. Here's what scientists say would happen.
parts.heard: Relax, it's only a thought experiment. Here's what scientists say would happen.

lines.text: First, nights get darker, like a new moon every single night.

parts.tts: First, nights get darker, like a new moon every single night.
parts.heard: First, nights get darker, like a new moon every single night.

lines.text: But the tides are the big one. The Moon does most of the pulling.

parts.tts: But the tides are the big one. The Moon does most of the pulling.
parts.heard: But the tides are the big one. The moon does most of the pulling.

lines.text: The Sun makes tides too, but it pulls less than half as hard.

parts.tts: The Sun makes tides too, but it pulls less than half as hard.
parts.heard: The sun makes tides too, but it pulls less than half as hard.

lines.text: So every tide would be roughly a third of today's.

parts.tts: So every tide would be roughly a third of today's.
parts.heard: so every tide would be roughly a third of today's.

lines.text: But animals would get confused. Some dung beetles steer by moonlight.

lines.text: They'd have to switch to steering by the Milky Way instead.

lines.text: But the strangest part is slow. Over a few hundred thousand years, Earth's tilt could wobble.

lines.text: Mars has no big moon... and its tilt swings by up to sixty degrees.
